summary: Practise social mapping, transect walks and ranking for rural project planning. Explore PRA training and its field-ready outputs.
lede: Participatory appraisal methods help practitioners gather and interpret community evidence for rural project planning. Designed for field facilitators, project officers and community engagement specialists, the course develops skills in preparing community profiles, facilitating social maps and transect walks, and building seasonal calendars. You will also practise ranking priorities, validating findings through triangulation, and linking community feedback to project actions.
audienceIntro: This course is for professionals who facilitate community-level assessment or use local evidence to shape rural development activities. It suits entry-level practitioners and those refreshing their approach to participatory fieldwork.
audience: Livelihoods Project Coordinators using household priorities
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with rural development projects or community-facing work is useful. No prior PRA facilitation experience is required.
topics: Data collection, survey design & mobile tools
